Some light reading: https://bitcoin.org/en/getting-started

Get a wallet to hold the bitcoin. Choose one from here: https://bitcoin.org/en/choose-your-wallet I'd start with the plan old Bitcoin Wallet on a mobile device and use small sums.

Find out who sells BTC in your country: http://howtobuybitcoins.info/

I like to use https://localbitcoins.com/ to find bitcoin ATMs near me and convert cash into BTC when I can. You can find a lot of other ways to get BTC here, but it will cost extra in $$ and risk. If there are no ATMs handy I use https://www.coinbase.com/ that is hooked into an https://www.ally.com/ bank account created just for bitcoin that I deposit USD into. (This requires you to prove ID to both entities) Anytime I buy on coinbase I immediately transfer it out to my personal wallets. There are many other sites like coinbase. http://bitcoinx.io/how-to-choose-the-right-bitcoin-exchange/ and many other options out there if you don't like that and don't want to link a bank account. Some places will let you do wire transfers, cash at a bank, money order, check and some recently even do credit cards (many don't as you could buy BTC, then call your bank and reverse the charges). https://coincafe.com/fees.php
https://www.expresscoin.com/how

Some rules of thumb:
* Backup your wallet, set a spending pin. Keep small sums in it you can afford to completely loose if you screw something up.
* Don't keep large sums on online exchanges you buy BTC from.
* Nothing is free, ever, and there are thieves... Everyone selling is trying to make money off of you somehow.
* You'll pay more $$ to get equivalent BTC and that amount will vary with the method used.
* Staring out, there's not really a surefire way to buy BTC and get it immediately, you have to wait. Unless you have a trusted friend that sells BTC.
* Don't consider bitcoin anonymous. You may not be known but all transactions are public and you could be tracked if a party is motivated to do so and ID you via other means

I just want to add to that. All the BTC, that I have bought, I got via localbitcoins.com, which is not an exchange, but a marketplace essentially. Localbitcoins doesn't sell any BTC, they only establish the connection between seller and buyer and hold the BTC in escrow to prevent buyers and sellers being scammed.

You don't need to prove ID on localbitcoins. Some sellers want to see ID, but I just ignore these and look for others. The way it works is this: You choose a seller based on his price(which is usually ~ 10USD above market price) or other trade parameters, enter the amount of BTC you want from him and start the transaction. His BTC are now put in escrow, locked down, waiting for you, so he can't sell them to somebody else. You will now see his bank details and are suppoded to wire the specified amount. Once he receives the wire, he tells localbitcoins and the BTC will be given to your localbitcoins wallet. From there it's advised to transfer the coins to a personal wallet on your computer or smarphone or paperwallet. I wouldn't advice online wallets. Alternatively you could also send the BTC directly to any other address, such as the voat donation adress, if that's the only reason you bought the coins.

If you are in Europe you can use SEPA and have your BTC the next day.

Buying on a site like coinbase may be faster and a little cheaper (market price) but the lack of providing ID on localbitcoins is worth it for me. You might differ in this regard.

Download Armory on Windows or BreadWallet on iOS, or Mycelium on Android and keep your funds there. I recommend BreadWallet. On those you get access to your private keys so it's your bitcoins, not Coinbase's bitcoins.

Since bitcoin is p2p, you download a wallet app. Look here. Don't get a wallet with "full verification," as that will download the full 40GB blockchain to your computer. I recommend electrum.

Basically what these wallets do is store your private key, which is a really big number that proves that you own your bitcoin. They also help you make transactions and view your balance.

The problem with keeping your bitcoin with a third party such as coinbase is that they control the key that proves you own the bitcoin, not you. What if they get hacked, or behave maliciously?

Bitcoin isn't hard to use, you just need to be computer literate and take 30 minutes to learn the basics of how it works and best practices.
